Sellside Analysts' Memo · Sdiptech · built 3 November 2026

How the sell-side sees Sdiptech, and where its view is heading

What each broker on record thinks and how that has moved over twelve months, with the Investment Analyst's judgement on where the sell-side goes next.

  • Three kinds of content, each labelled. The brokers' own commentary, from 37 research reports produced between 27 May 2026 and 31 Oct 2026 (blue-edged cards). The Investment Analyst's reading of the sell-side, from its Layers 1 to 4 and three memos (purple-edged cards and the judgement boxes). This memo's summaries, tables and charts, which name their sources.
  • Breadth. 1067 passages from 15 research houses, plus consensus and investor views. Every house the research records on this stock is included, however briefly it appears.
  • Checks. Every quotation was matched word for word to its source by script, every summary sentence was checked against the passages, and every number survived the editing.
How current this is, and what was left out

The research covers AlphaSense reports produced between 27 May and 31 Oct 2026, with broker note titles back to 2018; the latest broker view on Sdiptech is RedEye's third-quarter review of 29 Oct 2026. The Investment Analyst's work is dated 29 to 31 Oct 2026, and the fourth-quarter report is due on 10 Feb 2027 (recorded in a report of 7 Oct 2026).

Two passages under Barclays and Jefferies are research questions that only name peers; they are used just for the macro point each attributes. Undated DNB Carnegie targets of SEK 280 and SEK 290, and rating splits that contradict the 100% Buy record, appear only under conflicts.

The answer in brief

  1. Two houses write on Sdiptech; FactSet counts two brokers, both at Buy.

    • DNB Carnegie and RedEye are the houses writing on Sdiptech directly, with 625 and 364 passages and note titles running to 26 and 29 Oct 2026.
    • FactSet counts two brokers, DNB Carnegie and Nordea, with a 100% Buy share unchanged over six months; the Investment Analyst writes that Coverage is very thin (29 Oct 2026).
    • No Sell or Underperform rating was found over the last 12 months, recorded in a report of 27 May 2026; one report of 20 Sep 2026 cites a different rating split (see conflicts).
    • Most positive: DNB Carnegie, with a Buy, the highest target (SEK 340) and the highest earnings per share forecasts (SEK 15.1, 19.5 and 22.0 for financial years 2026 to 2028).
    • Least positive on numbers: Nordea (earnings per share SEK 12.1, 16.2, 18.9) and RedEye (base case fair value SEK 315). Twelve other houses comment on currencies, rates, economies, sectors or peers rather than on Sdiptech's shares; Bernstein adds one Sdiptech margin estimate and Modular Finance compiles consensus.
    Source: Passage counts; FactSet revisions file; Investment Analyst's Layer 1 and Layers 3 and 4; earnings review of 29 Oct 2026; DNB Carnegie and RedEye note titles.

  2. Note titles moved from restructuring and currency worries to steady, positive delivery.

    • Twelve months ago titles were hopeful: DNB Carnegie's Q3 better than feared, gearing up for 26e earnings recovery and RedEye's Stable core becoming increasingly visible (both 27 Oct 2025).
    • January to February 2026: DNB Carnegie's Organic growth acceleration clouded by FX (28 Jan) gave way to Restructuring soon forgotten; bluer skies ahead (11 Feb); RedEye wrote Incremental improvements (12 Feb).
    • April to May 2026: DNB Carnegie's Revenge is in the air (9 Apr) and Comeback story still very much intact (29 Apr); RedEye's Strategic pivot completed, growth engine restarted (4 May 2026).
    • July to October 2026: Divestments done and strong organic growth (DNB Carnegie, 20 Jul), Step by step in the right direction (RedEye, 22 Jul) and Another quarter in the right direction (DNB Carnegie, 26 Oct).
    • Latest title: RedEye's Sales beat, Base Case raised to SEK315 (29 Oct 2026). No title in the twelve months records a lower rating.
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye note titles (ledger).

  3. DNB Carnegie's target rose from SEK 290 to SEK 340; RedEye's base case from SEK 280 to 315.

    • DNB Carnegie cut its target to SEK 290 from SEK 315 on 28 Jan 2026, then raised it to SEK 305 (9 Apr), 310 (29 Apr), 330 (11 Jun) and 340 (20 Jul).
    • DNB Carnegie trimmed its target to SEK 340 from SEK 342 after the third quarter on lower peer multiples, recorded in a report of 29 Oct 2026; the SEK 342 is unexplained (see conflicts).
    • RedEye's base case fair value, which is not a target, went from SEK 270 (cut in October 2025) to SEK 280, SEK 290 (28 Apr or 4 May 2026; see conflicts), SEK 300 (22 Jul) and SEK 315 (29 Oct 2026).
    • Nordea's target was SEK 325 on 17 Jul 2026 and SEK 327 on 2 Oct 2026, with a Buy, according to the Investment Analyst's records.
    • The FactSet consensus target rose from SEK 274.83 (16 Jun 2026) to a mean of SEK 302.50 (18 Sep) and about SEK 313 (29 Oct); targets are up 10% over six months.
    Source: Change Forces report of 20 Sep 2026; earnings review of 29 Oct 2026; RedEye passages and note titles; Investment Analyst's broker records and readings; FactSet revisions file.

  4. Brokers stopped framing a restructuring case and started framing a restarted compounder.

    • Early 2026 was defensive: DNB Carnegie cut its financial year 2026 earnings per share 15% in January 2026 on an analyst change and currency, recorded in a report of 27 May 2026.
    • DNB Carnegie said the improvements were positive but would temporarily label Sdiptech as a restructuring case, recorded in a report of 8 Jun 2026.
    • RedEye had cut its base case 10% after the third quarter of 2025, alongside a SEK 500m goodwill write-down on legacy service businesses, recorded in a report of 3 Jun 2026.
    • By mid-2026 both houses framed a restart: RedEye's title Strategic pivot completed, growth engine restarted (4 May 2026); DNB Carnegie's Korsheden argued the restructuring was ending, triggering an asymmetric risk/reward re-rating, recorded in a report of 8 Jun 2026.
    • In October the debate moved to profit drop-through: RedEye set organic EBITA growth of 6% against 13% organic sales growth in the third quarter (29 Oct 2026).
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages; RedEye note title.

  5. Both houses agree the clean-up left a higher-quality core and restarted acquisitions.

    • DNB Carnegie argued on 26 Oct 2026 that selling 11 non-core subsidiaries left a much cleaner, higher-quality group focused on high-margin niches.
    • RedEye stressed the divestments were done at an average 6.7 times EBITA and removed lower-margin service noise, recorded in an earnings review of 8 Aug 2026.
    • Acquisitions have restarted: DNB Carnegie puts the Wheels and Castors and Vale Engineering deals at SEK 40m of run-rate profit against a SEK 100m annual target (report of 29 Oct 2026).
    • DNB Carnegie expects 8% acquired growth a year through 2032 (report of 20 Sep 2026); RedEye builds about SEK 100m of acquired EBITA a year into its forecasts (29 Oct 2026).
    • Both warn on deal competition: RedEye's Knutsson said more serial acquirers could compress returns; DNB Carnegie said Addtech and Lifco can outbid Sdiptech for quality United Kingdom targets (26 Oct 2026).
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages; earnings reviews of 8 Aug and 29 Oct 2026.

  6. Organic growth beat expectations; both houses expect it to slow, and frame the slowdown differently.

    • Third-quarter 2026 organic growth of 13% beat DNB Carnegie's 6% forecast; DNB Carnegie called it the fifth consecutive quarter of organic acceleration (26 Oct 2026).
    • DNB Carnegie said on 13 Oct 2026 that any slowdown reflects tougher comparisons rather than a weakening of core operational momentum.
    • DNB Carnegie also cautioned on 13 Oct 2026 that orders postponed from 2025 cannot recur as a permanent driver, and that sustainable organic growth should revert toward 6%.
    • RedEye models organic growth of 10.7% in 2026, 6.0% in 2027 and 3.0% from 2029 (29 Oct 2026).
    • A report of 30 Oct 2026 reads RedEye's forecast as showing that only select analysts anticipate the deceleration, leaving the wider consensus unprepared; this is the report's inference, not RedEye's words.
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages.

    Organic growth beat, but both houses expect a slowdown

    Third-quarter organic growth of 13% beat DNB Carnegie's 6% forecast, yet DNB Carnegie expects sustainable organic growth to revert toward 6%, and RedEye models 6.0% in 2027.

  7. Margins, United Kingdom costs and leverage are the worries both houses share.

    • RedEye flagged a third-quarter gross margin of 58.1% against its 61.4% estimate (29 Oct 2026); one report says the fall is raising questions about true pricing power.
    • DNB Carnegie warned on 26 Oct 2026 that Supply Chain & Transportation margins stay under pressure in the fourth quarter and that Safety & Security margins are unsustainable.
    • United Kingdom exposure: DNB Carnegie notes about 49% of sales are in the United Kingdom, leaving earnings exposed to sterling and to United Kingdom wage inflation (26 to 29 Oct 2026).
    • Leverage: RedEye reported net debt at 2.95 times adjusted EBITDA, near the 3.0 times ceiling; DNB Carnegie said 2.95 times leaves virtually no covenant headroom (26 to 29 Oct 2026).
    • DNB Carnegie still projects leverage falling from 3.0 times in 2026 to 2.0 times in 2027 and 1.4 times in 2028, recorded in an earnings review of 29 Oct 2026.
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages; earnings review of 29 Oct 2026.

    Leverage sits at the covenant ceiling

    Net debt is 2.95 times adjusted EBITDA, near the 3.0 times ceiling; DNB Carnegie says this leaves virtually no covenant headroom, though it projects 2.0 times in 2027.

  8. Financial year 2027 consensus earnings per share is up 8% over six months.

    • FactSet financial year 2027 earnings per share rose 2% over one month, 7% over three, 8% over six and 3% over twelve (read 29 Oct 2026), to SEK 17.73; the Investment Analyst's memo has (0.6)% over twelve months (see conflicts).
    • Financial year 2027 sales consensus rose 3%, 4% and 8% over one, three and six months but is (4)% over twelve; EBITDA rose 1%, 2%, 5% and 1%.
    • Earlier years were cut hard: financial year 2026 earnings per share is still (12.6)% over twelve months, and the Investment Analyst records that FY2025 consensus EPS fell 44.5% over twelve months.
    • FactSet median earnings per share is SEK 14.06, 17.66 and 19.19 for 2026 to 2028, with DNB Carnegie and Nordea 20% to 25% apart (Investment Analyst, 29 Oct 2026).
    • RedEye sits outside FactSet: its 2027 earnings per share of SEK 15.85 is 11% below consensus because it models future deals and their financing, while its 2027 sales are 6% above.
    Source: FactSet revisions file (read 29 Oct 2026); Investment Analyst's Layer 1 and memo; RedEye passages.

  9. Both houses call the discount to Swedish compounders too wide, but partly deserved.

    • DNB Carnegie puts Sdiptech at 11.1 times 2027 enterprise value to EBITA against Lagercrantz at 21.0 times and Addtech at 19.4 times, a discount difficult to justify (26 Oct 2026).
    • DNB Carnegie's method: a 10% discount to peers and a re-rating toward 13.5 times; a separate acquisition scenario gives a fair value of SEK 366, which is not its target (see conflicts).
    • DNB Carnegie earlier called 11 to 12 times 2026 enterprise value to EBITA a junk multiple, recorded in a report of 27 May 2026.
    • RedEye shows 12.4 times 2026 enterprise value to EBITA, a 37% discount to a 16.8 times peer median, and says a discount over 25% is too wide (29 Oct 2026).
    • Both concede part of the discount: RedEye cites leverage near 3.0 times; DNB Carnegie cites lower return on capital employed and past restructuring (26 to 29 Oct 2026).
    Source: DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages; earnings review of 29 Oct 2026.

  10. Investors were sceptical before the re-rating; brokers say the clean-up revived interest.

    • Before the re-rating, the market expected low organic growth and high leverage to constrain near-term earnings, recorded in a report of 10 Jun 2026.
    • DNB Carnegie said the end of restructuring was reigniting institutional interest; RedEye's Knutsson said the divestments almost completely erased a perceived risk among investors (reports of 8 and 10 Jun 2026).
    • DNB Carnegie noted on 26 Oct 2026 that the stock had outperformed peers by 35% since June.
    • One report warned that unanimous Buy views signal severe consensus groupthink that downplays United Kingdom and interest-rate risks (report of 8 Jun 2026).
    • The Investment Analyst records the shares +23.1% over twelve months, +45.9% over nine (28 Oct 2026) and notes The top ten holders are near 50% of capital.
    Source: Investors and consensus passages; DNB Carnegie and RedEye passages; Investment Analyst's Layers 3 and 4.

  11. The Investment Analyst expects consensus to rise, in steps, over 18 months.

    • The Investment Analyst's judgement (30 Oct 2026) on consensus: More likely higher than lower, in steps rather than a trend.
    • The Investment Analyst's memo (31 Oct 2026) states: Consensus is more likely to rise than fall over 18 months; its Layers 3 and 4 note that acquisitions not in consensus are a point DNB Carnegie has made since at least March 2026.
    • The Investment Analyst finds the narrative thin in voices and uneven in content; its September memo called the sell-side two houses at 100% buy, which is crowding.
    • On valuation, the Investment Analyst writes The market is at 13.5x; the brokers at 16x to 17x: the market figure is on 24-month-forward earnings, the brokers' figure is their targets measured on the Investment Analyst's own financial year 2027 to 2028 earnings.
    • The September memo (22 Sep 2026) judged upgrades probable over the next six to twelve months, but rated them B rather than A because the twelve-month financial year 2026 revision was still (10.7)%.
    Source: Investment Analyst's Layers 3 and 4 (30 Oct 2026), memo (31 Oct 2026) and September memo (22 Sep 2026).

Where the sell-side's view is heading

The Investment Analyst's judgement

The Investment Analyst judges the cutting over: the sell-side is early in an upgrade phase, with estimates rising in steps as acquisitions arrive.

  • Twelve months: financial year 2027 consensus earnings per share is up only 3% and sales are down (4)%; in June the Investment Analyst still found revisions uniformly negative beyond one month.
  • Six months, the turn: earnings per share rose 8%, sales 8%, EBITDA 5% and the target price 10%; the Investment Analyst dates the turn to the second-quarter 2026 report, after the 2025 reset.
  • Three months and one month: earnings per share rose 7% over three months but 2% over one; targets rose 3% in each; the Buy share held at 100%. The Investment Analyst sees slowing.
  • What turned it: organic growth ran ahead of broker forecasts once the cutting ended: DNB Carnegie had 6% organic growth in the third quarter against 13% actual.
  • Where next: the Investment Analyst judges financial year 2027 consensus more likely higher than lower, with 60% odds of a rise of 3% or more by February 2028, in steps.
  • Why: consensus models no unannounced acquisitions; each deal lifts next year's earnings per share by about 0.7% per SEK 10m of operating profit, so the Investment Analyst expects upgrades deal by deal.
  • What would prove it wrong: fourth-quarter cash conversion below 90% would cut the Investment Analyst's upgrade probability to 40%; with two brokers, one downgrade would be half the consensus.

What each broker says

Each research house in turn, ordered by how much the research records from it: its view in one line, then how it frames the case, its arguments, its worries and how its view changed. Quoted words are the research report's.

DNB CarnegieCarl Korsheden, Robert RedinBuy, target SEK 340 (26 Oct 2026, trimmed from SEK 342)

DNB Carnegie is the most positive house: Buy throughout, target raised to SEK 340 in 2026, and a case that a cleaner core deserves a re-rating.

Stance and how it got there

  • Buy throughout: co-analyst Robert Redin kept a Buy through 2025 and 2026, recorded in a report of 8 Jun 2026; Carl Korsheden took over lead coverage from Niklas Ekman and Victor Hansen.
  • Target path: SEK 315 to SEK 290 on 28 Jan 2026 (currency and divestment timing), then SEK 305, 310, 330 and 340 between 9 Apr and 20 Jul 2026.
  • After the third quarter DNB Carnegie reiterated Buy and trimmed its target to SEK 340 from SEK 342 on lower peer multiples, recorded in a report of 29 Oct 2026.

How it frames the case

  • A comeback story: titles run from Revenge is in the air (9 Apr 2026) to Comeback story still very much intact (29 Apr) and Another quarter in the right direction (26 Oct).
  • Restructuring ending: DNB Carnegie argued the restructuring saga was ending sooner than expected, which should erase the stock's complexity discount, recorded in a report of 27 May 2026.
  • Best risk-reward: DNB Carnegie considers Sdiptech the best risk/reward opportunity among Swedish compounders (report of 20 Sep 2026) and kept it in its small-cap core pick portfolio on 2 Oct 2026.

Main arguments

  • Higher-quality core: selling 11 non-core units leaves EBITA margins above 20% and lets investors refocus on the profitable, non-cyclical core (26 Oct 2026).
  • Organic acceleration: 13% organic growth in the third quarter of 2026 was the fifth consecutive quarter of acceleration, which DNB Carnegie calls a key supportive pillar (26 Oct 2026).
  • Cheaper financing: the September 2026 bonds lower the cost of debt (13 Oct 2026); a report of 29 Oct 2026 says DNB Carnegie raised later-year earnings per share 5% on lower net financial items (other reports differ; see conflicts).
  • Upside skew: DNB Carnegie says the clean-up makes the forecast cone narrower and more skewed to the upside than history suggests, unless a credit freeze halts deals (26 Oct 2026).

What worries it

  • United Kingdom and sterling: about 49% of sales are in the United Kingdom, leaving earnings exposed to sterling, and DNB Carnegie warns United Kingdom wage inflation will keep margins under pressure (26 Oct 2026).
  • Leverage and cash: net debt of 2.95 times adjusted EBITDA leaves virtually no covenant headroom, and DNB Carnegie models only 55% long-term cash conversion (26 Oct 2026).
  • Acquisition discipline: DNB Carnegie calls acquisitions the primary risk and notes Sdiptech historically paid higher acquisition multiples than peers (reports of 27 May and 8 Aug 2026).
  • Segment margins: Supply Chain & Transportation stays under pressure in the fourth quarter and the Safety & Security margin is unsustainable, according to DNB Carnegie on 26 Oct 2026.

How its view changed

  • Over 12 months: DNB Carnegie moved from estimate cuts (financial year 2026 earnings per share down 15% in January 2026) and a SEK 290 target to SEK 340 by July 2026.
  • Over 6 months: a report of 27 May 2026 describes DNB Carnegie's revisions as a clear pivot from technical downgrades to structurally confident upgrades.
  • Over 3 months: the target held at SEK 340 (apart from the SEK 342 in conflicts) while 2027 earnings per share rose from SEK 18.6 (report of 20 Sep 2026) to SEK 19.5 (26 Oct 2026), with more margin caveats.

RedEyeStefan Knutsson, Martin WahlströmNo formal rating or target; base case fair value SEK 315, bear case SEK 170, bull case SEK 435 (29 Oct 2026)

RedEye is constructive but more cautious than DNB Carnegie: its base case is now SEK 315, and it stresses gross margin, leverage and a 2027 slowdown.

Stance and how it got there

  • Base case, not a target: RedEye publishes a base case fair value with bear and bull cases; one report of 3 Jun 2026 describes its stance as Buy or equivalent.
  • Base case path: cut to SEK 270 in October 2025, then SEK 280, SEK 290 (28 Apr or 4 May 2026; see conflicts), SEK 300 (22 Jul 2026) and SEK 315 (29 Oct 2026).
  • Scenario range: bear case SEK 170 and bull case SEK 435 after the third quarter, up from SEK 170 to 410 (recorded in a report of 8 Aug 2026); these are scenario values, not targets.

How it frames the case

  • Pivot and restart: RedEye's titles read Strategic pivot completed, growth engine restarted (4 May 2026) and Step by step in the right direction (22 Jul 2026).
  • Rare steady growth: RedEye says steady organic growth is rare among serial acquirers because Sdiptech's units hold strong niche positions, recorded in a report of 30 Oct 2026.
  • A different model: RedEye models future, unannounced deals, so its 2027 sales run 6% above consensus while its 2027 earnings per share of SEK 15.85 is 11% below (29 Oct 2026).

Main arguments

  • Clean-up done well: RedEye says divestments at an average 6.7 times EBITA removed lower-margin service noise, recorded in an earnings review of 8 Aug 2026.
  • Valuation: RedEye says the discount is partly justified by leverage and flat margins, but a peer discount of over 25% is too wide (29 Oct 2026).
  • Cheaper funding: RedEye cut its cost of capital to 9.1% from 9.3% after the bond refinancing, helping lift the base case to SEK 315 (29 Oct 2026).
  • Deals restarting: RedEye says A.U.T. and VALE Engineering add about SEK 40m of acquired operating profit (29 Oct 2026).

What worries it

  • Gross margin: RedEye says the third-quarter 2026 gross margin of 58.1% missed its 61.4% estimate, a third consecutive miss, and calls the cost base structurally higher (29 Oct 2026).
  • Drop-through: RedEye says organic EBITA growth of 6% against 13% organic sales growth suggests difficulty passing on inflationary inputs (29 Oct 2026).
  • Leverage and earn-outs: RedEye reports net debt up to 2.95 times adjusted EBITDA, and listed earn-outs of SEK 205m (rest of 2026), SEK 162m (2027) and SEK 392m (2028 to 2029) on 22 Jul 2026.
  • 2027 slowdown: RedEye models organic growth of 10.7% in 2026 and 6.0% in 2027, which a report of 30 Oct 2026 reads as showing that only select analysts anticipate the deceleration.
  • Return on capital: RedEye noted on 27 Oct 2025 that return on capital employed averaged 11% over four years, short of the 15% target.

How its view changed

  • Over 12 months: RedEye went from a 10% base-case cut after the third quarter of 2025, alongside a SEK 500m goodwill write-down, to three dated base-case raises in 2026 (to SEK 290, 300 and 315).
  • Over 6 months: the 4 May 2026 title marked the turn; RedEye's Knutsson called leverage of 2.81 times comfortable for resuming acquisitions, recorded in a report of 29 Oct 2026.
  • Over 3 months: RedEye raised the base case to SEK 315 and sales forecasts 3% to 5%, but grew more cautious on gross margin and on leverage, up from 2.80 to 2.95 times.

Where the brokers disagree

Will organic growth hold up in 2027?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie said on 13 Oct 2026 that any slowdown comes from tougher comparisons, not weaker momentum, and on 26 Oct that the forecast cone is skewed to the upside.
  • DNB Carnegie forecast on 16 Oct 2026 that 2027 could see 15% EBITA growth including recent acquisitions.
  • RedEye says steady organic growth is rare among serial acquirers because Sdiptech's units hold strong niche positions (report of 30 Oct 2026).

The more negative side

  • RedEye models organic growth falling from 10.7% in 2026 to 6.0% in 2027 and 3.0% from 2029 (29 Oct 2026).
  • One report, citing RedEye's 29 Oct 2026 update, says part of the momentum is a timing shift and may unwind in the first half of 2027.
  • DNB Carnegie itself cautioned on 13 Oct 2026 that postponed 2025 orders cannot recur and that sustainable organic growth should revert toward 6%.

Can Sdiptech turn sales growth into profit growth?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie expects strong operating leverage and margin expansion now that low-margin units are gone (26 Oct 2026), and says price indexation projects are under way (report of 29 Oct 2026).
  • RedEye notes other external and personnel costs fell in the third quarter, which one report reads as pointing to gross margins returning to historical levels; one unit fully passed through material costs (29 Oct 2026).

The more negative side

  • RedEye says the 58.1% gross margin missed its 61.4% estimate and the cost base is structurally higher (29 Oct 2026).
  • RedEye sets 6% organic EBITA growth against 13% organic sales growth (29 Oct 2026), and reports Water & Bioeconomy's margin down to 20.1% from 20.9%, a higher cost base that management calls the new normal.
  • DNB Carnegie warns Supply Chain & Transportation margins stay under pressure in the fourth quarter and Safety & Security margins are unsustainable (26 Oct 2026).

Is the valuation discount to Swedish compounders deserved?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie calls 11.1 times 2027 enterprise value to EBITA, against 21.0 times at Lagercrantz, difficult to justify (26 Oct 2026); a report of 27 May 2026 records it calling 11 to 12 times 2026 enterprise value to EBITA a junk multiple.
  • RedEye shows a 37% discount to the peer median and says anything over 25% is too wide (29 Oct 2026).

The more negative side

  • DNB Carnegie says the discount reflects lower return on capital and past restructuring and will persist without consistent margin execution (26 Oct 2026).
  • DNB Carnegie sees no premium multiple until leverage falls below 2.0 times; RedEye sees the multiple capped near 11 times until cash deleverages the balance sheet (report of 31 Oct 2026).
  • RedEye says leverage near the 3.0 times limit justifies part of the discount (29 Oct 2026).

Does leverage constrain the acquisition restart?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie projects leverage falling from 3.0 times in 2026 to 2.0 times in 2027 and 1.4 times in 2028 (report of 29 Oct 2026).
  • DNB Carnegie says earn-outs fall 40% if profits stay flat, offsetting weaker cash and preventing covenant breaches (26 Oct 2026).
  • RedEye's Knutsson called leverage of 2.81 times comfortable for resuming acquisitions, recorded in a report of 29 Oct 2026.

The more negative side

  • RedEye reports leverage up to 2.95 times, near the 3.0 times ceiling, and says a breach would cripple deal-making (29 Oct 2026).
  • DNB Carnegie says 2.95 times leaves virtually no covenant headroom and models only 55% cash conversion (26 Oct 2026).
  • RedEye lists earn-outs of SEK 205m, SEK 162m and SEK 392m falling due from late 2026 to 2029 (22 Jul 2026).

How much does Sdiptech earn, and will consensus catch up with acquisitions?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie forecasts earnings per share of SEK 15.10, 19.50 and 22.00 for 2026 to 2028 (26 Oct 2026) and says deals drive revisions because consensus excludes them.
  • RedEye models unannounced acquisitions, so its 2027 sales are 6% above consensus; one report says this could trigger major consensus upgrades (report of 30 Oct 2026).

The more negative side

  • Nordea forecasts SEK 12.10, 16.20 and 18.90 (October 2026), which one report calls a major discount to other estimates.
  • RedEye's 2027 earnings per share of SEK 15.85 is 11% below consensus, because it charges financing and amortisation for modelled deals (29 Oct 2026).
  • One report says inconsistent methods across brokers create false precision in consensus (report of 30 Oct 2026).

How large a risk are the United Kingdom economy and sterling? (largely macro houses commenting on the economy, not on Sdiptech)

The more positive side

  • Rothschild & Co Redburn called the United Kingdom budget a tiny net tightening, and noted the Office for Budget Responsibility raised its growth forecast to 1.2% (report of 30 Oct 2026).
  • Morgan Stanley says the Planning and Infrastructure Bill aims to unlock stalled projects; Deutsche Bank held a constructive sterling view (reports of 29 Oct and 3 Jun 2026).

The more negative side

  • DNB Carnegie says about 49% of sales are in the United Kingdom, so sterling and wage inflation threaten earnings (26 Oct 2026).
  • Deutsche Bank reported the weakest July brick deliveries in forty years and possible frozen public budgets (report of 29 Oct 2026); Jefferies noted a 3.9% wage-floor rise for April 2027.
  • Morgan Stanley holds a bearish skew on sterling, and Maybank warns of stagflation risk for sterling (report of 3 Jun 2026).

Will data-centre and grid demand keep supporting growth?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie noted on 8 Sep 2026 that Eagle has a filled data-centre security order book, which one report reads as making infrastructure demand a 2027 growth engine.
  • Morgan Stanley says data-centre capacity could grow 14% a year through 2030; ING expects utility spending above two hundred billion euros in 2027 (report of 30 Oct 2026).

The more negative side

  • DNB Carnegie flags high order concentration (8 Sep 2026) and possible tightening credit for data-centre automation (23 Oct 2026).
  • ING warns a hyperscaler slowdown would halt component orders; Morgan Stanley notes digital investment is only 3% of euro-area output (report of 30 Oct 2026).
  • DNB Carnegie and RedEye both expect the Safety & Security margin to come down; RedEye models about 32% (26 and 29 Oct 2026).

Where the research reports conflict. Both versions are shown; this memo does not pick one.
  1. DNB Carnegie's target before the third-quarter review: SEK 340 or SEK 342.
    • One version: DNB Carnegie set SEK 340 on 20 Jul 2026 and reaffirmed it on 8 Sep; the Investment Analyst records DNB Carnegie SEK 340 on 4 Sep 2026.
    • Other version: an earnings review of 29 Oct 2026 says Korsheden lowered the target to SEK 340 from SEK 342.
    • Not settled: when, or whether, DNB Carnegie moved to SEK 342; the Investment Analyst's memo cites broker targets of SEK 313 to 342.
  2. DNB Carnegie's acquisition-scenario fair value: SEK 366 or SEK 435.
    • One version: DNB Carnegie's separate seven-year acquisition scenario gives SEK 366 a share (reports of 29 and 30 Oct 2026; also the Investment Analyst).
    • Other version: a report of 6 Oct 2026 says DNB Carnegie's scenario (2 Oct 2026) indicates SEK 435, the same figure as RedEye's bull case.
    • Not settled: whether SEK 435 was DNB Carnegie's earlier scenario value or RedEye's figure misattributed. Neither is a target.
  3. Undated DNB Carnegie targets of SEK 280 and SEK 290.
    • One version: a report of 8 Jun 2026 says DNB Carnegie maintains a target valuation of SEK 280; a report of 10 Jun 2026 says Korsheden held SEK 290.
    • Other version: dated records show DNB Carnegie at SEK 310 from 29 Apr and SEK 330 from 11 Jun 2026.
    • Not settled: neither report dates its figure; SEK 290 matches DNB Carnegie's target between 28 Jan and 9 Apr 2026, but SEK 280 matches no recorded DNB Carnegie target.
  4. DNB Carnegie's mid-October 2026 estimate changes.
    • Version one: on 16 Oct 2026 DNB Carnegie cut 2026 earnings per share 1% to SEK 15.1 and raised 2027 and 2028 by 5% on cheaper financing; a report of 29 Oct 2026 gives the same 5% rise with a 2% cut for 2026.
    • Version two: a report quotes the same 16 Oct note as cutting 2026 by 2%, 2027 by 4% and 2028 by 3% on higher financing costs.
    • Version three: after the third quarter (26 Oct 2026) changes were (1)% for 2026, zero for 2027 and +1% for 2028. The inputs do not reconcile these.
  5. Rating split: 100% Buy or some Hold and Sell.
    • One version: FactSet shows a 100% Buy share, and reports of 27 May and 3 Jun 2026 found no Sell or Underperform ratings in the last 12 months.
    • Other version: a report of 20 Sep 2026 cites a 59% Buy share, 38% Hold, and 3% Sell as of late 2025 per DNB Carnegie, and refers to sceptical hold and sell arguments.
    • Not settled: whether the 59% figure describes Sdiptech or a wider universe; no Hold or Sell house on Sdiptech is named.
  6. DNB Carnegie as a source of the bearish narrative.
    • One version: a report of 3 Jun 2026 says The bearish narrative is primarily driven by respected Nordic brokers like DNB Carnegie.
    • Other version: DNB Carnegie kept a Buy throughout and raised its target four times between April and July 2026.
    • Not settled: the report may mean DNB Carnegie's estimate cuts and risk lists, which coexisted with its Buy.
  7. RedEye: rating and target, or base case and range.
    • One version: the Investment Analyst's June memo lists RedEye (Buy, TP SEK 290); a report of 3 Jun 2026 says RedEye holds a Buy or equivalent.
    • Other version: RedEye's own figures are base case fair values with bear and bull cases, for example SEK 300, SEK 170 and SEK 410 (report of 20 Sep 2026).
    • Range figures also differ for April to June 2026: SEK 170 to 380, SEK 160 to 400, and a bear case of SEK 150 are all recorded.
  8. Date of RedEye's raise to SEK 290: 28 Apr or 4 May 2026.
    • One version: a report of 20 Sep 2026 dates the raise from SEK 280 to SEK 290 to 28 Apr 2026, RedEye's first-quarter initial take.
    • Other version: reports of 8 Jun and 20 Sep 2026 date the same raise to 4 May 2026, RedEye's first-quarter review.
  9. Multiple implied by DNB Carnegie's SEK 340 target.
    • Versions: 14 times 2027 enterprise value to EBITA (report of 6 Oct 2026), 15.3 times (report of 7 Oct 2026), 13.5 times (29 Oct 2026) and 13.6 times (31 Oct 2026).
    • Not settled: the reports may use different years or bases; the Investment Analyst puts the brokers' targets at 16 to 17 times its own earnings forecasts.
  10. Twelve-month revision of financial year 2027 consensus earnings per share.
    • One version: the FactSet revisions file read on 29 Oct 2026 shows rises of 2%, 7% and 8% over one, three and six months and 3% over twelve.
    • Other version: the Investment Analyst's memo, with data of 28 Oct 2026, shows the mean up 3.9%, 7.3% and 9.6% over one, three and six months but (0.6)% over twelve.
    • Not settled: the two may measure different statistics; both show rises of 7% or more over three and six months.
